timing_interpretation.rule: usage.prompt_tokens is total input usage (cached plus uncached); native prompt_n is the native prompt interval count (the uncached portion when reuse happened) and cache_n is the independent reuse counter, both verbatim. The compatible split check is prompt_n + cache_n against the total input usage per the native llama.cpp contract; cache is never subtracted twice. Native prompt rates and wall-clock prompt estimates are scoped to their compatible interval: full prompt only with native no-reuse evidence (cache_n == 0) without a contradicting total, the uncached/native interval under reconciled reuse, otherwise UNKNOWN. A cached-interval rate is never presented as a full-prompt rate; negative counters and unreconciled splits produce no derived rates; metering findings compare compatible quantities; missing evidence stays UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE, never zero. Historical finalized evidence retains its original accounting

limitations: native prompt throughput on these repeats meters the native prompt interval; full-prompt processing coverage is established only by native no-reuse evidence (cache_n == 0)
